title: NIST CSF 2.0 maturity
heading:
How mature is your
NIST CSF 2.0 posture?
lead: Six quick questions across the NIST Cybersecurity Framework functions give you an instant read on your overall maturity and where to focus first.

items.name: Govern
items.q: Is cyber risk governed, with clear ownership, policy, and leadership oversight?
opts: No real governance. Cyber is nobody's clear responsibility.
Informal. Some policy exists but ownership is unclear.
Documented policy with an accountable owner and regular review.
Board-level oversight, measured against risk appetite, continually improved.

items.name: Identify
items.q: Do you have a current view of your assets, data, and risks?
opts: No inventory or risk register.
A partial or out-of-date inventory.
A maintained asset inventory and a living risk register.
Continuous, largely automated discovery with prioritised risk.

items.name: Protect
items.q: Are safeguards in place (access control, MFA, hardening, training)?
opts: Minimal safeguards beyond the defaults.
Some controls, applied inconsistently.
Consistent controls across the estate, including MFA and hardening.
Strong, least-privilege controls that are tested and enforced everywhere.

items.name: Detect
items.q: Can you detect suspicious or malicious activity across your environment?
opts: No real monitoring.
Basic logging, rarely reviewed.
Centralised monitoring and alerting that reaches a person.
24/7 detection enriched with threat intelligence and threat hunting.

items.name: Respond
items.q: Do you have a tested incident response capability?
opts: No plan.
An informal, undocumented approach.
A documented incident response plan with defined roles.
A plan that is regularly tested, with clear roles and communications.

items.name: Recover
items.q: Can you recover systems and data after an incident?
opts: No reliable backups.
Backups exist but are not tested.
Automated, tested backups and a recovery process.
Proven recovery that consistently meets your recovery objectives.
